title: Remember the capture temporary directory as a preference
description:
Wireshark and TShark can be told where to put temporary capture files
(--temp-dir, or the Capture Options dialog), but the choice is never
remembered - anyone whose root filesystem is small, or who keeps captures
on a separate disk, has to set it again every session. This adds a
preference for it and routes the GUI's own scratch files through the same
setting.

Two commits:

- Capture: Add a preference for the temporary directory
  Registers capture.temp_dir as a directory preference and uses it as the
  default for capture_opts->temp_dir. It is only a default: an empty value
  means "no preference" (system default applies), and --temp-dir / the
  Capture Options dialog still win over it. The option parser gains a flag
  recording that the value came from the preference, so seeding it does not
  turn a command-line --temp-dir into a "given twice" error. The directory
  reaches dumpcap through the existing capture_sync path, so the large
  capture files land where they were asked to. TShark copies the one field
  itself rather than pulling in ui/preference_utils.c (and the GUI with it).

- Qt: Honour the capture temporary directory for scratch files
  The RTP player and the IAX2 analysis dialog wrote their decoded audio to
  QDir::tempPath(), ignoring the setting above. They now use a small Qt
  wrapper over the same capture_opts_get_temp_dir() the C side uses, so the
  two cannot drift, and the About dialog's Folders tab reports the directory
  that will actually be used. Two QDir::tempPath() callers are left alone on
  purpose - export_object and the traffic-map HTML are handed to another
  program, which may not be able to read a directory chosen for Wireshark's
  own scratch space.

commits_data.title: Qt: Honour the capture temporary directory for scratch files
commits_data.message:
Qt: Honour the capture temporary directory for scratch files

The RTP player and the IAX2 analysis dialog write their decoded audio
to temporary files, and both asked QDir::tempPath() where to put it.
That ignores --temp-dir, the Capture Options dialog and the
capture.temp_dir preference, so someone who has pointed Wireshark at a
roomier disk still had these files land somewhere else. Decoded audio
for a long call is not small, and /tmp is not always the right place
for it.

Add a Qt tempPath() beside the other UI helpers, returning the
directory the user asked for and falling back to QDir::tempPath(), and
use it for those four files. It is a thin wrapper over the same
capture_opts_get_temp_dir() the C side uses, so the two cannot drift
apart, and it keeps the HAVE_LIBPCAP conditional in one place rather
than in every dialog.

The two open-coded copies of "the directory if one was set, otherwise
the system default" go too: the capture options log now calls
capture_opts_get_temp_dir(), and the About dialog's Folders tab calls
tempPath(), so the tab reports the directory that will actually be
used. The About dialog has to go through tempPath() rather than call
capture_opts_get_temp_dir() directly, since the latter only exists in
builds with libpcap.

Two callers of QDir::tempPath() are deliberately left alone:
export_object_dialog writes a file for the system handler to open, and
traffic_tab writes an HTML map for a browser. Those are handed to
another program, which may not be able to read a directory the user
chose for Wireshark's own scratch space, and neither grows with the
capture.

Assisted-by: Claude
Signed-off-by: Peter Lemenkov <lemenkov@gmail.com>

commits_data.title: Capture: Add a preference for the temporary directory
commits_data.message:
Capture: Add a preference for the temporary directory

TShark and Wireshark can already be told where to put temporary
capture files, with --temp-dir or the field in the Capture Options
dialog, but neither is remembered. Anyone whose root filesystem is
small, or who keeps captures on a separate disk, has to say it again
every session.

Register capture.temp_dir as a directory preference and use it as the
default for capture_opts->temp_dir. An empty preference means "no
preference", leaving the directory unset so the system default still
applies. Because it is only a default, --temp-dir and the Capture
Options dialog continue to win over it.

That precedence needs the option parser to know where the current
value came from. --temp-dir refuses a second use, and a value seeded
from the preference would otherwise look like a first use and make
every --temp-dir on the command line an error, so capture_options
gains a flag recording that the directory is a preference default.
Giving --temp-dir twice is still rejected.

TShark copies the one field itself rather than calling
prefs_to_capture_opts(): it cannot link ui/preference_utils.c, which
drags in simple_dialog() and the rest of the GUI, and applying the
remaining capture preferences to TShark would be a behaviour change
beyond this one.

The preference reaches dumpcap as well, since capture_sync already
forwards the directory to it, so the capture files that are large
enough to matter land where they were asked to.

Assisted-by: Claude
Signed-off-by: Peter Lemenkov <lemenkov@gmail.com>
